p: Got a favourite animal? Make it your first stop. Crowd-pleasers include Land of the Lions, Tiger Territory, Gorilla Kingdom and Penguin Beach, while the walk-through Monkey Valley inside the old Snowdon Aviary is a real treat.

Remember the Regent's Canal splits the zoo into two halves, linked by bridges and a tunnel, so glance at the map before you set off to avoid doubling back. Weekends and school holidays get busy, so turning up for opening time buys you a calmer first hour with the gorillas and lions.

Regent's Park itself is worth exploring before or after your visit. Queen Mary's Gardens has a beautiful rose garden with thousands of roses that bloom in summer, perfect for a peaceful stroll. In summer, the Regent's Park Open Air Theatre puts on plays and musicals under the stars, a magical experience for families.

For a different view, take a canal boat along the Regent's Canal between Little Venice and Camden, passing the zoo along the way. Fans of a certain detective can pop to Baker Street, at the south-western corner of the park, where the Sherlock Holmes Museum recreates the famous 221b flat.

The zoo has some famous former residents too. Jumbo, the giant African elephant whose name became a word for anything huge, lived here in the 19th century, and a black bear called Winnipeg, or Winnie for short, charmed a young Christopher Robin Milne and inspired the name of Winnie-the-Pooh. Look out for the statue of Winnie as you go round.
